concept: One meeting room drawn like a small paper stage set, five people behind one long table under a locked camera, and four private doubts (a checklist, a headset, a sealed envelope, a calendar page) folded in bubbles only the viewer can see: in the first meeting they stay folded while every hand goes up, weeks later they come true on the same objects, and in the rewound meeting each habit turns one doubt into a written note on the table, until the opening frame returns with all four said. Moving right is forward in time (the room, weeks later, the viewer's week); below is the naming page; the viewer's week holds Dana's room inside one meeting slot.

story.metaphor: none forced (soft skills): the meeting itself is the stage, and each private doubt is drawn as an object in a folded bubble only the viewer sees
story.setting: one meeting room round one long table, a board on the left wall, a window on the right; once weeks later on a dark field; once the viewer's own week, which holds the room in one meeting slot
story.arc: the vote first, then rewind to how it happened (leader first, a fast yes, four hidden doubts, each thinks they are alone, hands up); the doubts come true; the name; rewind; the same meeting with four habits, each bringing one doubt to the table; your turn; your week; the opening frame with the doubts on the table

cast.role: the leader: reasonable and well meaning, never a villain; the only named person

cast.name: the fast yes
cast.role: the colleague beside Dana who agrees first; privately doubts the date

cast.name: the testing colleague
cast.role: privately knows testing is not done

cast.role: privately knows support is not trained; the named critic in the replay

cast.name: the person by the window
cast.role: privately knows the client has not seen it

devices.what: one locked meeting room (the set bible) held across beats while its state changes on the word: hands, bubbles, board, plan, notes; reframed only by cuts (wide, medium left, close right, medium right), never by drifting

four private doubts as drawn objects in folded wobble bubbles over the four colleagues; folded, open, folded and sealed are one outline morphing (Loom.morph.to), stepped on fours, with one red mark per doubt

each habit arrives as a teal tag or object on the thing that does it, and its doubt drops from the bubble to the table, the object's outline morphing into a note card with its one word; the notes collect in front of their owners where the stamp was

the board's writing area is a Loom.slot: the words on it are relabelled or swapped on the spoken word (goal, blank, premortem page, the plain lesson), so the team's shared surface carries the argument

the vote on fours: arms rise one per step, poses held between steps (Loom.stepped.on hz 6), the Agreed stamp lands; shown as the result b02, repeated with its cause b07, run backwards b12, and answered by cards written and turned at once b14 and b19

the one join material: torn paper, used only for jumps in time, its edge read as a calendar page being torn off (the date doubt's own material); right is forward (b08, weeks later), left is back (b12, rewind)

value_script.why: a pale, quiet open: a paper room in near monochrome with colour withheld; the only saturated marks are the four thin red seams on the folded bubbles
the story proper sits slightly richer: the leader's goal in ochre on the board, then the doubts in red as they open (b05); b06 narrows the light to four pools inside this band
the failure: the field drops to dark ink paper and only the red failure marks are saturated; the dark carries into the room after it (b09). The lesson's one dark break, kept for the consequence
the dip to black is the turn; the naming page and the notes come back up to paper, and the rewound meeting (b12 to b16) stays in this band while the notes arrive
the lift: the plan gets fixed and the room brightens back to the open's pale band for the practice
colour withheld until the payoff: the four red notes sit together on the table in the lightest frame of the film, the ochre plan beside them

stations.note: SET BIBLE (station coords 1920x1080; drawn IDENTICALLY wherever the room appears: 'room' in b01 to b07, b09, b12 to b17; 'meet' in b19 and b21). Walls and floor: ctx.scenery('room', 'set', {window: true, windowX: 1440, floor: 0.70}) (wall to y 756, window x 1440 to 1862, y 151 to 540, one slow cloud drift in the glass as the ambient loop, period 4.8 s). Board 'board': x 300 to 720, y 150 to 420, surface fill, ink frame, pen tray; its writing area is a Loom.slot (frame 'none') at x 330 to 690, y 180 to 390, so every change of words on it is a relabel or swap on the spoken word. Clock 'clock': Loom.obj clock (wall) at (1080, 180), size 90. Table 'table': top polygon, back edge y 640 from x 420 to 1620, front edge y 790 from x 320 to 1720 (surface2, ink outline), front panel y 790 to 840 (shadow token); drawn IN FRONT of the people so it hides them below the hips. People (ctx.character, scale 0.44, feet y 760 hidden by the table, so they read as seated): 'dana' rig tess x 560; 'p_date' (the fast yes) rig pip x 790; 'p_test' rig tess x 1020; 'p_support' rig pip x 1250; 'p_client' rig tess x 1480 (by the window). Vary skin and hair between them; tops in quiet tokens only (muted, shadow, field2, surface2): no saturated cloth, the accents are reserved. Dana standing = same x, raised 90 px. Bubbles (the four colleagues only, never Dana): 'bub_date', 'bub_test', 'bub_support', 'bub_client'. Folded: centred (owner x + 40, 330), about 80 x 60, the seed's wobble outline with a crease line and a thin red (accent) seam, two tail dots down to the head. Open: centred (owner x + 30, 270), about 180 x 150, holding the object (about 90 px) with its one-word tag under it. Objects 'obj_date', 'obj_test', 'obj_support', 'obj_client': a calendar page (Loom.obj calendar tearoff) with a red question mark; a half-ticked checklist (Loom.obj document clipboard, 2 of 4 boxes ticked, the empty boxes edged red); a headset (no Loom.obj kind: kit shapes, band arc, two ear cups, a mic boom with a red tip; an object, not a figure); a sealed envelope (Loom.obj envelope flap with a red wax seal). Plan sheet 'sheet': lying on the table, centre (1135, 750), about 220 x 80 in perspective, paper with ink lines and a small calendar glyph; header strip ochre (accent2) only while the plan is the named thing. In the first meeting it drifts to (1065, 750) in b04 and stays there until b12 slides it back. Note slots (sec2 and the payoff) 'note_date', 'note_test', 'note_support', 'note_client': on the table in front of each owner, centre (owner x, 666), card about 150 x 76, slight seeded tilt, surface paper, a red tape strip, the word lettered in the display face (label role, ink). Stamp 'stamp': 'Agreed' in accent2 ink, about 180 x 64, tilted minus 8 degrees, on the plan sheet. Colour meanings for the whole lesson: accent (brick red) = a doubt (seams, marks, failure, notes); accent2 (ochre) = the plan and the decision (goal, stamp, amended plan); accent3 (teal) = a habit (the critic tent card, the habit tags). Never more than two of them saturated in a settled frame. Hand-made time: Loom.stepped.on (hz 6) on the people and the drawn props, Loom.stepped.boil (hz 8, amp about 1.2) on outlines during holds; never on text, captions or the camera. No hands kit anywhere (placeholders): arms are the rigs' own stick limbs.
weeks later: the four doubt objects on a dark ink-paper field (b08); to the right of the room because it is later in time
the naming page on the paper field: the term card (b10) and the meeting's notes (b11); below the story because it is the idea under it
the viewer's week as a wall planner (b20), Monday to Friday, blank meeting blocks; the Wednesday block at (760, 420, 400, 225) holds the nested station 'meet'
Dana's room again, nested in the week's Wednesday block (b19, b21); drawn with the 'room' set bible, same coordinates

scenes.subject: five people round one table, each with a folded private doubt
scenes.accent_on: the four folded bubbles' red seams

design.treatment: The whole room, locked wide, built from the set bible; the place is present at frame 0 with no entrance (TED-Ed opens on a composed tableau; the picture speaks first). The five small outlined people settle into their seats behind one long table in stepped time (two drawings each, not a slide), the plan sheet gets its tag, and then the private doubts arrive: a folded wobble bubble above each of the four colleagues, one per step, each with one thin red seam, the only colour in the frame. Dana, at the left end under the board, has none. From 'Nobody says so' to the end, the bubbles' outlines boil gently so the held tableau is never frozen.
design.why_motion: the hook is a change the viewer sees and the characters cannot: private doubts appearing over a table where nothing is said. The doubts arriving one by one IS the line 'each one doubts it'.
elements: the five people behind the table (rigs tess and pip, seated)
the plan sheet with its tag 'one plan'
four folded bubbles, one red seam each
(world, not counted) the room: wall, board, clock, window with its cloud drift, table

a paper tag 'one plan' pins to the sheet's corner and is written on

beat_sheet.action: every gaze returns to the front; the bubbles' outlines start a boil that runs to the end of the beat

design.treatment: The same locked wide frame, everything held. Open on the result, then show it happening: on 'Agreed' the ochre stamp slams onto the plan sheet; on 'Every hand goes up' the five raise one arm each, one per step, left to right, Dana first, each arm pose HELD between steps rather than tweened (stepped hz 6; the rig's raised-arm pose, no wave gesture). design.treatment: Cut to the medium frame on Dana, the board and the plan sheet (the room is held through the cut: same station). First the meeting rewinds to its start: on 'Meet Dana' the stamp peels off and leaves, the arms come down in three stepped drawings and the clock's minute hand ticks back. A paper name tag 'Dana' pins beside her. She stands (two stepped drawings) and turns to the board, and her goal is lettered onto it as she says it, 'Launch:' then 'end of quarter' on a second line, in ochre. The colleagues in frame turn their eyes to the board one per step. She is warm and reasonable: an open, presenting pose, never a pointing one.

design.treatment: Cut closer, along the table, to the four colleagues and their bubbles (Dana is out of frame: the leader cannot see them either). Each folded bubble opens on its own words: its outline MORPHS from the folded shape to the open wobble bubble (Loom.morph.to, about 0.9 s, stepped at hz 8 so it reads drawn), then its object draws in (outline first, fill after) with its one-word tag lettered under it. The order follows the narration, not the seats: testing, support, client, and last the fast yes on the far left, the surprise 'even'. Each object carries one small red mark (the unticked boxes, the mic tip, the wax seal, the question mark). Nobody looks up: each person looks at the table or towards the board, never at a bubble.
design.why_motion: what each person privately holds is the lesson's central picture, and it must arrive one doubt at a time, on its words (bubble_with_changing_content, externalised_inner_state)

scenes.subject: each doubter deciding they are the only one
scenes.world: Dana's meeting room: the private doubts
scenes.accent_on: the bubbles' red seams as they fold shut

design.treatment: The slowdown, on a held close frame. Each colleague's eyes glance left, then right, in stepped looks, one person after another: what each one sees is calm faces and the backs of bubbles they cannot read. On 'Calm faces' every face settles neutral and the light narrows: a soft veil darkens the wall and leaves four pools of light, one on each person (still inside the mid band). On 'I must be the only one' the four bubbles fold shut one after another: each outline morphs from open back to folded and swallows its object, leaving only the red seam. A small paper tag 'the only one?' hangs from the last bubble to fold, the fast yes's, and is written on as it is said.
design.why_motion: the hinge of the lesson (F9, F16) is a decision each person makes alone and in turn: look, see calm, fold the doubt away. Slow stepped glances are the slowdown the pedagogy asks for
elements: the bubbles folding shut, one by one

the wall darkens by about 25 percent around four soft pools on the people

scenes.subject: the four doubts coming true on the same objects
scenes.world: weeks later: the doubts come true

design.treatment: A torn-paper wipe crosses left to right: the time jump, its torn edge read as a calendar page torn off. Behind it, a dark ink-paper field (the lesson's one dark break) with the four doubt objects in the seats' order, large, in a row at x 270, 730, 1190, 1650, y 520, each about 300 px, built as ONE motif group ctx.motif('doubts') so b09 can carry them back. On 'Weeks later' the calendar's pages tear off one per step (three pages, each falling away with a small turn). On 'the launch slips' the date on the last page is crossed out in red and a paper tag 'launch slips' pins to it. On 'Every one of those doubts comes true' the other three fail in seat order, one per half second: red crosses fill the checklist's empty boxes, the headset rings (red ring lines boil round it, the cups shake in two drawings), the envelope comes back with a red return arrow drawn round it. Every outline boils to the end of the beat.
design.why_motion: the consequence is a sequence in time, and it must land on the SAME objects the viewer saw in the bubbles, so the failure is recognised rather than explained
elements: calendar losing pages, the date crossed out
envelope returned with a red arrow

design.treatment: The camera travels back left to the room (travel join, carried by the doubts motif). The room is redrawn from the set bible at frame 0, with no entrance, under a dark veil: the dark band continues. The five sit as before, arms down, calm, no bubbles. The doubts motif flies in during the join and settles in a row above the four colleagues, each object hanging on a thin string from the top of the frame, still marked red. On 'Nobody in that room was foolish' nothing is added: calm faces, the strings sway slightly (a period-locked ambient loop, 4 s). On 'Every doubt was right' a paper strip 'every doubt was right' clips onto the middle string. On 'None of them reached the table' a dashed drop line draws down from each object towards the table and stops short, leaving a clear gap above the tabletop, one per step: the gap is the lesson.

scenes.subject: the first meeting running backwards

design.treatment: A torn-paper wipe crosses right to left: time going back. Behind it the room is redrawn exactly as b07 left it (arms up, lids pressed flat, the Agreed stamp, Dana standing, her goal on the board, the sheet drifted). On 'Keep those four doubts in mind' all four lids show a faint glimpse of their objects at once (a ghost silhouette inside, one 0.5 s gesture, not one per step, because the beat is only about 3 s): the recall prompt. On 'Now, rewind' everything runs backwards in quick stepped drawings, like flipped pages (Loom.stepped.wrap, hz 8): the clock's hands spin back with a tag 'rewind' pinned to the clock, the stamp lifts off, arms come down, the lids spring back into folded bubbles, the goal un-writes from the board right to left, Dana sits, the sheet slides back to the middle. It ends on the opening state: a clear board and four folded bubbles waiting.
design.why_motion: the rewind is time running backwards, and it sets up the replay: same people, same room, only the habit will change

scenes.subject: everyone writing a view first, and the testing doubt coming out

design.treatment: Cut to the wide frame. Five blank cards slide onto the table, one in front of each person, as one gesture (tight stagger, 0.08 s), and a teal tag 'Write before you talk' pins to the table's front edge. All five heads tilt down together and ink scribble lines appear on all five cards at once (stepped, the lines boil): everyone writing at the same moment. On 'Out comes' all five cards flip together; four show scribbles, the one in front of the testing colleague shows the half-ticked checklist with its red empty boxes. That card's outline morphs into the note 'testing' beside 'the date', the other four cards slide back, and the testing colleague's folded bubble shrinks to a point and is gone.
design.why_motion: independent views (F14) are a timing claim: everyone writes at the same moment, so nobody follows anybody; the simultaneous flip IS the habit

design.treatment: Cut into the room, redrawn from the set bible in station 'meet'. It is the next meeting: Dana stands at the board, which carries her view as ink scribble lines (the next plan is not named, so no words), no notes, no bubbles, a quiet room. On 'Speaking last is gone. She spoke.' the scribbled view greys out (recolour to muted) and a small teal tag 'speak last' beside it is crossed through. On 'Asking again asks someone to go first' one colleague's arm starts to rise alone, the light narrows onto them, a paper tag 'go first?' hangs above, and the arm comes back down (stepped): going first alone is the cost. On 'everyone writes why it could fail' Dana writes 'write: why could it fail?' on the board and five cards slide out together, heads down, scribbles appearing at once (the b14 device returning). On 'Then they read them out' all five cards flip at the same moment, several showing a small red mark: the doubts arrive together and nobody goes first.
design.why_motion: the answer is a timing claim: writing first (F14) aimed like a premortem (F15) brings every doubt out at the same moment, while asking again asks one doubter to go first alone (F9, F16)
